question: Simplify : (1 - (1)/(costheta)) ( (1 + sectheta)/(tan²theta) )
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use identities: secθ = 1/cosθ and tan²θ = sec²θ − 1

(1 − 1/cosθ) = (cosθ − 1)/cosθ and (1 + secθ) = (1 + 1/cosθ)

Convert everything in terms of cosθ

After simplification, expression reduces neatly

**∴ Answer = −1**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(1 − 1/cosθ) ( (1 + secθ)/tan²θ )

**Formula used:**

secθ = 1/cosθ, tan²θ = (1 − cos²θ)/cos²θ

**Calculation:**

⇒ Replace secθ = 1/cosθ

⇒ = (1 − 1/cosθ) × ((1 + 1/cosθ)/tan²θ)

⇒ = ((cosθ − 1)/cosθ) × ((cosθ + 1)/cosθ) × (1/tan²θ)

⇒ = (cos²θ − 1)/cos²θ × (1/tan²θ)

⇒ = (−sin²θ)/cos²θ × (cos²θ/sin²θ)

⇒ = −1

**∴ The correct answer is −1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Trigonometric Identities

secθ = 1/cosθ and tanθ = sinθ/cosθ

Pythagorean Identity

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

Derived Identity

tan²θ = sin²θ / cos²θ

Simplification Tip

Convert all terms into sine and cosine for easier cancellation.
